approved: Ending Poverty in Australia (Antipoverty Commission) Bill 2023
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create a permanent, independent body to advise Parliament on poverty and social security payments.
The Antipoverty Commission would run reviews of poverty levels and payment adequacy, with its leaders chosen by a parliamentary committee.
The government would be required to publicly answer the Commission's recommendations.
Establishes the Antipoverty Commission as a legislated, independent advisory body.
Requires the Commission to conduct antipoverty reviews and social security payment reviews.
Mandates that the government publicly respond to the Commission's recommendations.
People living in poverty, recipients of income support, and the Australian Parliament and government.
